issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap, drop policy, or time bound.
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list[LogRecord] retained from _on_setup until flush or cleanup. A slow-hanging job or chatty DEBUG library can balloon memory before anyone notices. Make it a bounded ring (size or bytes) with an explicit drop policy. State the invariant: buffer holds at most N records or M bytes.

issues.description: OTLP handler located by isinstance scan over root logger handlers; silent no-op if scan fails.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer scans logging.getLogger().handlers for the first LoggingHandler instance and breaks. Coupling to global mutable state and handler ordering means replay silently drops every buffered record if assumptions break — precisely the bug this PR claims to fix. Hold the handler returned by _setup_cloud_tracer by reference on JobContext and address it directly.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry strips every LoggingHandler from the root logger as a global side effect.
issues.detail: The deadlock fix removes all opentelemetry LoggingHandler instances from root before force_flush, taking any user-installed handler of that type as collateral. Scope removal to the handler this module installed, by reference, not by type scan. State the re-entrant emit path the slice-copy defends against so a future maintainer does not reintroduce the deadlock.

issues.description: _shutdown_fut overloaded to carry both crash signaling and orderly shutdown semantics.
issues.detail: _on_entry_done forces _shutdown_fut with reason='job crashed' on any task exception, conflating crash with user/timeout shutdown on the same channel. Consumers branching on shutdown_info now see broader meaning. Use a typed reason (CRASH vs USER vs TIMEOUT) or a separate signal so the future's postcondition is not silently widened.

issues.description: _on_cleanup re-enters init_recording with unreasoned interaction with prior recording state.
issues.detail: Cleanup conditions on `_early_log_handler is not None and not _recording_initialized` then calls init_recording, which itself stops buffering if already initialized or url is not cloud. The branch is unreasoned: if a prior init_recording failed leaving _recording_initialized=True with no OTLP handler, buffered records are silently dropped with no audit trail. State the precondition or log dropped count.

issues.description: Unrelated changes bundled without justification (makefile -n auto, google STT test exclusion, worker.py reorder, test_ipc edits).
issues.detail: Dropping pytest-xdist parallelism, excluding test_plugin_google_stt.py, reordering _pending_assignments registration before _queue_msg, and the test_ipc retry-batch change are separate facts of the world bundled with the crash-log feature. Each may be correct but the bundling defeats reasoning and reverts. Split or annotate why.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR addresses a real defect — crash logs lost when sessions fail to start — but the implementation accretes complexity in the logging subsystem without stating its invariants. The buffered handler is unbounded, the OTLP sink is located by isinstance scan over global root-handler state (silent no-op on failure), and _shutdown_telemetry mutates global logging state as a broad side effect. _shutdown_fut is overloaded to carry crash signaling alongside orderly shutdown semantics. Unrelated changes to makefile, worker.py, and tests are bundled without justification. Verdict: needs a bounded buffer, handler-by-reference, narrower shutdown scope, and the unrelated changes split out before merge.
